title: Getting started with olympicAthletes
text: Medals olympic_athletes per-player: every member gold-winning ice hockey roster medal = "Gold" row. right shape athlete-level analysis, inflates team counts sum naively. headline medal-table totals, use medal_table instead.
code: # Every roster member of the men's ice hockey gold medal team # at Beijing 2022 gets a Gold row: hockey_2022 <- subset(   olympic_athletes,   year == 2022 &     event == "Ice Hockey Men's Ice Hockey" &     medal == "Gold" ) nrow(hockey_2022) #> [1] 0

title: Getting started with olympicAthletes
text: medal_table covers every Olympic edition Athens 1896 Milano-Cortina 2026 uses IOC per-team-event convention. Top five NOCs Paris 2024 gold count:
code: data(medal_table) head(subset(medal_table, year == 2024), 5) #>      edition_id       games year season noc                    country gold #> 1808         63 2024 Summer 2024 Summer USA              United States   40 #> 1809         63 2024 Summer 2024 Summer CHN People's Republic of China   40 #> 1810         63 2024 Summer 2024 Summer JPN                      Japan   20 #> 1811         63 2024 Summer 2024 Summer AUS                  Australia   18 #> 1812         63 2024 Summer 2024 Summer FRA                     France   16 #>      silver bronze total notes #> 1808     44     42   126       #> 1809     27     24    91       #> 1810     12     13    45       #> 1811     19     16    53       #> 1812     26     22    64 paris <- subset(medal_table, year == 2024) paris <- paris[order(-paris$gold, -paris$total), ] head(paris[, c("noc", "country", "gold", "silver", "bronze", "total")], 5) #>      noc                    country gold silver bronze total #> 1808 USA              United States   40     44     42   126 #> 1809 CHN People's Republic of China   40     27     24    91 #> 1810 JPN                      Japan   20     12     13    45 #> 1811 AUS                  Australia   18     19     16    53 #> 1812 FRA                     France   16     26     22    64

title: olympicAthletes • Athens 1896 to Milano-Cortina 2026
text: olympic_athletes extends original rgriff23/Olympic_history dataset. Column names lowercase snake_case (e.g. noc, medal) rather upstream TitleCase, host-city column split city_local_latin city_english. city_local_latin always uses Latin alphabet — non-Latin-script cities romanized ("Moskva", "Tokyo", "Beijing", "PyeongChang"), rendered native script.
code: library(olympicAthletes)  data(olympic_athletes)   # ~315,000 athlete-event rows, 1896-2026 data(medal_table)        # verified medal table for every edition, 1896-2026 data(editions)           # metadata for every Games, 1896-2026  # Convenience subsets of olympic_athletes (same 16 columns) data(athletics_athletes)       # sport == "Athletics" data(gymnastics_athletes)      # sport == "Gymnastics" data(basketball_athletes)      # sport == "Basketball" data(olympic_athletes_2024)    # Paris 2024 Summer Games only data(team_sport_athletes)      # Basketball + Volleyball + Curling data(art_competitions_athletes)  # the 1912-1948 Art Competitions entrants data(usa_summer_medals)        # medal_table rows: USA at each Summer Games  # Tidy medal summary for barplot teaching examples (long format) data(paris_2024_top_medals)    # top-10 countries x Gold/Silver/Bronze  ?olympic_athletes

title: olympicAthletes • Athens 1896 to Milano-Cortina 2026
text: Medal counts per-player, per-team-event. team gold (e.g. Ice Hockey Men) produces one medal = "Gold" row per roster member. Group medal noc divide team-event medals team size reproduce IOC medal table — use medal_table companion dataset uses IOC convention. Bio coverage: v0.4.0 bio refresh, age ~100% complete five 2018-2026 editions. height/weight coverage ranges 96%/93% 2018 Winter 34%/29% Paris 2024 — highest Winter team sports (Ice Hockey rosters near-complete olympedia) lowest largest, -recent Summer Games, olympedia simply hasn’t published measurements many athletes — pattern original 1896-2016 source.

title: Edition-level metadata for every Olympic Games, 1896-2026 — editions
text: data frame 62 rows 15 variables: edition_id Integer. Olympedia's internal edition number. games Character. e.g. "2024 Summer". year Integer. season Character. "Summer" "Winter". city_local_latin Character. Host city local-language     form rendered Latin alphabet — .e. native Latin-script     names retain diacritics ("Athína", "München",     "Montréal", "Ciudad de México"), non-Latin-script     names use standard romanization rather city's native     script ("Moskva" "Москва", "Tokyo"     "東京", "Beijing" "北京",     "PyeongChang" "평창"). column therefore     always ASCII--Latin-1 never contains city's     native non-Latin alphabet. city_english Character. Common English name host city     (e.g. "Athens", "Munich", "Moscow",     "Mexico City"). country Character. opening_ceremony, closing_ceremony Date NA. ISO-8601.     NA cancelled editions early Games     Olympedia record exact dates. participants Integer NA. Olympedia's headline     participant count. NA cancelled editions. nocs Integer NA. Number NOCs represented. medal_events Integer NA. Number medal events. disciplines Integer NA. Number distinct disciplines. notes Character. Free-text edition notes (e.g. cancellation     reasons, intercalated-Games status). source Character. Olympedia URL.

title: Olympic athlete-event participations, 1896-2026 — olympic_athletes
text: data frame 315,094 rows 16 variables: id Integer. Unique athlete ID. Original IDs 1..135571;     athletes new 2018-2026 editions get IDs starting     1,000,000 avoid collision. name Character. ASCII-folded athlete name. sex Character. "M" "F". age Integer NA. Approximate age start     Games, computed date birth (Feb 1 reference Winter,     Jul 15 Summer). height Numeric NA. Height centimetres. weight Numeric NA. Weight kilograms. team Character. Country/team name displayed source. noc Character. Three-letter IOC code (e.g. "USA",     "", "ROC"). games Character. "<year> <Summer/Winter>", e.g.     "2026 Winter". year Integer. Calendar year Games. Tokyo 2020     coded 2020 even though held 2021 (IOC convention). season Character. "Summer" "Winter". city_local_latin Character. Host city local-language     form rendered Latin alphabet — .e. native Latin-script     names retain diacritics ("Athína", "München",     "Montréal", "Ciudad de México"), non-Latin-script     names use standard romanization rather city's native     script ("Moskva" "Москва", "Tokyo"     "東京", "Beijing" "北京",     "PyeongChang" "평창"). column therefore     always ASCII--Latin-1 never contains city's     native non-Latin alphabet. city_english Character. Common English name host city     (e.g. "Athens", "Munich", "Moscow",     "Mexico City"). sport Character. Sport name. 2018-2026 rows normalised     original sport names possible (e.g. "Cycling Track"     "Cycling Road" collapse "Cycling"). event Character. Event name including sport prefix. medal Character NA. "Gold", "Silver",     "Bronze", NA. Per-player: every member     medal-winning team roster gets row team's medal.

title: olympicAthletes 0.5.6
text: Removed olympic_athletes_2000_2026 (1.4 MB — second-largest file package) bring built package back CRAN’s 5 MB source-package guideline. pure subset olympic_athletes (year >= 2000); recreate time olympic_athletes |> filter(year >= 2000). ModernDive exercises used now use team_sport_athletes, athletics_athletes, explicit filter(). Removed olympic_athletes_1960 (referenced nowhere book, exercises, teaching materials); recreate olympic_athletes |> filter(year == 1960, season == "Summer").

title: olympicAthletes 0.5.5
text: Add three exercise-support subsets ModernDive Chapter 2 exercises (predate dplyr) never need base-R subsetting workarounds: usa_summer_medals (30 rows — one per Summer Games USA attended; note boycotted 1980 Games row), art_competitions_athletes (3,578 rows — 1912-1948 Art Competitions entrants), team_sport_athletes (10,912 rows — Basketball, Volleyball, Curling combined, cross-group distribution comparisons).

title: olympicAthletes 0.5.4
text: Renamed recent_olympic_athletes olympic_athletes_2000_2026 clearer, time-explicit name. data unchanged (year >= 2000, .e. 2000–2026 Games).

title: olympicAthletes 0.5.3
text: Add volleyball_athletes (4,792 rows) curling_athletes (961 rows) convenience subsets, parallel existing basketball_athletes / gymnastics_athletes, ModernDive Chapter 5+ regression examples.

title: olympicAthletes 0.5.2
text: Recovered missing noc/team (country) values: rows country unknown athlete (id) appears another Games known country now backfilled (unambiguous cases ). Reduces NA noc 10,094 3,907 rows; rest athletes never appear known country, competed one NOC, deliberately left NA.

title: olympicAthletes 0.5.1
text: New dataset paris_2024_top_medals: ten countries won total medals Paris 2024 Summer Games, long format (one row per country--medal-type: country, noc, medal, count). small, tidy dataset built barplot examples (stacked, dodged, proportional) without filtering ~90 medal-winning nations medal_table.

title: olympicAthletes 0.5.0
text: New single-Games convenience datasets: olympic_athletes_2024 (Paris 2024 Summer Games) olympic_athletes_1960 (Rome 1960 Summer Games). 2024 subset small enough show -plotting height vs weight scatterplot without full dataset’s scale; paired near-complete 1960 subset supports generational comparisons athlete physiques. columns identical olympic_athletes.

title: olympicAthletes 0.4.0
text: New convenience datasets: athletics_athletes, gymnastics_athletes, basketball_athletes (single-sport subsets olympic_athletes), plus recent_olympic_athletes (Games since 2000, year >= 2000). let teaching examples focus one sport recent Games without filter(). Columns identical olympic_athletes. olympic_athletes bio coverage substantially improved five olympedia-scraped editions (2018-2026). Team-event multi-athlete-row athletes (Ice Hockey, Curling, Bobsleigh, Football, Hockey, Rowing, relays, doubles, pairs, …) previously age mostly height/weight; bios now fetched olympedia. age now ~100% complete across five editions, height/ weight coverage rose accordingly (e.g. 2018 Winter height ~81% -> ~96%, Paris 2024 ~24% -> ~34%). refresh purely additive — row count, athlete roster, medal counts unchanged. editions: Tokyo 2020 participants corrected 11,319 -> 11,318 match olympedia’s revised count.

title: olympicAthletes 0.3.0
text: Breaking: olympic_athletes columns now lowercase snake_case (id, name, sex, age, height, weight, team, noc, games, year, season, sport, event, medal), matching convention already used medal_table editions. upstream rgriff23 TitleCase headers (ID, Name, NOC, …) longer preserved. Host-city columns now come local-language English forms. olympic_athletes, City column replaced city_local_latin city_english. editions, city replaced city_local_latin city_english. city_local_latin always uses Latin alphabet — Latin-script names keep native diacritics ("Athína", "München", "Montréal", "Ciudad de México") non-Latin-script names use standard romanization ("Moskva", "Tokyo", "Beijing", "PyeongChang") rather city’s native script.

title: olympicAthletes 0.2.0
text: medal_table now covers every Olympic edition Athens 1896 Milano-Cortina 2026 (1,929 rows, 273). Two new columns: edition_id (Olympedia’s internal edition number) notes. editions now covers every Olympic edition Athens 1896 Milano-Cortina 2026, including cancelled Games (62 rows, 5).

title: olympicAthletes 0.1.0
text: Initial release. olympic_athletes — 314,749 athlete-event rows spanning Athens 1896 Milano-Cortina 2026, extending rgriff23 Olympic_history dataset (1896-2016) five additional editions scraped olympedia.org. medal_table — 273-row verified medal table five new editions (2018, 2020, 2022, 2024, 2026), one row per (Games, NOC). editions — 5-row metadata table covering opening/closing dates, participants, NOC count, medal events, disciplines new edition.
